opportunities.title: Junior Scientist Conference Grant

amount.raw: Scheme A up to £200; Scheme B up to £500 (Adelphi co-sponsored up to £750); Scheme C up to £300

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics Society 'junior scientist' members. Scheme A open to undergraduate, Master's and PhD student members and postdoctoral members within six years of PhD viva. Schemes B & C open to PhD student and postdoctoral members within six years of PhD viva. Applicants must present a poster or give a talk at the conference.
opportunities.summary: Supports attendance of Genetics Society junior scientist members at conferences on research in Genetics. Three streams: (A) attendance at Genetics Society/SIG meetings (travel & accommodation, up to £200); (B) attendance at non-Genetics Society meetings (travel, accommodation, registration, up to £500, or up to £750 for Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored awards); (C) registration costs for virtual conferences (up to £300).

opportunities.title: Training Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society studying or working in the UK, or where the course is held in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year. Supervisors must be GS members.
opportunities.summary: Grants to enable members to attend formal short training courses, or a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic/genomic techniques. Covers travel, accommodation, subsistence, and registration/tuition fees.

opportunities.title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society studying or working in the UK, or intending to carry out fieldwork in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year. Supervisors must be GS members.
opportunities.summary: Covers travel and accommodation costs associated with field-based genetic research projects. Research should produce results suitable for publication in the journal Heredity. Funded by income from the Society's journal Heredity.

opportunities.title: Carer's Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any Genetics Society member, regardless of age of the person they are caring for. Priority given to early-career scientists and according to need.
opportunities.summary: Provides an award of up to £60/day to support members with caring responsibilities to attend Genetics Society meetings and events. Applied for prior to the meeting and competitive.

opportunities.title: One-off Meeting Grant

amount.raw: Several levels: a specific lecture for a few hundred pounds, a session up to about £1,000, major sponsorship of an entire meeting several thousand pounds (recent major sponsorships £1,000-£2,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics Society members. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of genetic-themed meetings not organised directly by the Genetics Society. Grants are used towards the organisation of a meeting (not attendance) and should include a Carer's Award. Applications may be made at any time of the year.

opportunities.title: Public Engagement Grant
opportunities.summary: Supports public engagement activities related to genetics, delivered in person or virtually. Funding may cover eligible travel and materials costs (UK-based, budget/economy class). Two deadlines per year (1st March and 1st October).

opportunities.title: Special Interest Group (SIG) Funding
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics research communities (Genetics Society members). Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of research meetings on particular themes for genetics research communities who wish to run regular series of meetings. Applications to become a new Special Interest Group should be submitted at least three months before the first meeting.
